items.followUp: Explain the organism and organ-system levels of biological organization.

rubric.why: These features distinguish a population from a collection of different species.
rubric.description: Defines a population and identifies where its members live.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for members of the same species and 1 mark for living in the same area or habitat.

rubric.why: A community consists of populations of different species living together in one place.
rubric.description: Defines a community and identifies its location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for different species or populations and 1 mark for living together in the same area or habitat.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
A community is made up of populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and functions of the nucleus.

rubric.why: The membrane's main structural components are a phospholipid bilayer and proteins.
rubric.description: Describes the membrane's basic composition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the phospholipid bilayer and 1 mark for membrane proteins.

rubric.why: Selective permeability allows the membrane to regulate the exchange of substances.
rubric.description: Explains selective permeability and control of transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for being selectively permeable and 1 mark for regulating movement into and out of the cell.

rubric.why: The orientation of phospholipids helps form the membrane bilayer.
rubric.description: States the arrangement of phospholipid parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the hydrophilic heads facing watery surroundings and hydrophobic tails facing inward.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane is a thin boundary surrounding the cytoplasm and separating the cell from its surroundings.
It is made mainly of a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
The hydrophilic heads of the phospholipids face the watery surroundings, while their hydrophobic tails face inward.
The membrane is selectively permeable and controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

items.followUp: Explain how biodiversity contributes to ecosystem stability and human welfare.

rubric.why: Biodiversity helps ecosystems remain stable and function effectively.
rubric.description: States the contribution of biodiversity to ecosystem stability.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking biodiversity with ecosystem stability.

rubric.why: Living organisms provide useful resources for people.
rubric.description: Gives examples of resources obtained from biodiversity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each of two valid resources or uses, such as food, medicines, timber, fuel or fibres.

rubric.why: Biodiversity supports important processes and services in ecosystems.
rubric.description: Names an ecosystem service supported by biodiversity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid service, such as pollination, soil formation or climate regulation.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity helps maintain the stability and proper functioning of ecosystems.
It provides useful resources, including food, medicines, fuel, timber and fibres.
It also supports ecosystem services such as pollination, soil formation and climate regulation.

items.followUp: Describe the role of light reactions in photosynthesis and name their main products.

rubric.why: Dark reactions occur in the stroma and use energy carriers produced by the light reactions.
rubric.description: Defines the dark reactions and identifies their location or energy source.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that these reactions do not directly require light and/or that they use ATP and NADPH in the stroma.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide is fixed by combining with RuBP, producing 3-PGA.
rubric.description: Describes carbon fixation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the combination of carbon dioxide with RuBP to form 3-PGA.

rubric.why: ATP and NADPH provide energy and reducing power to convert 3-PGA into G3P (PGAL).
rubric.description: Describes the reduction stage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for conversion of 3-PGA into G3P or PGAL using ATP and NADPH.

rubric.why: Some G3P contributes to carbohydrate formation, while the remaining material is used to regenerate RuBP.
rubric.description: States the fate of G3P and the regeneration of RuBP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that G3P or PGAL is used to make glucose or carbohydrates and 1 mark for regeneration of RuBP.

modelAnswer: Dark reactions, also called the Calvin cycle, are the light-independent reactions of photosynthesis that occur in the stroma and use ATP and NADPH from the light reactions.
Carbon fixation: carbon dioxide combines with RuBP to form an unstable six-carbon compound, which splits into 3-PGA molecules.
Reduction: ATP and NADPH are used to convert 3-PGA into G3P (also called PGAL).
Some G3P is used to form glucose and other carbohydrates.
The remaining G3P is used, with energy from ATP, to regenerate RuBP.

items.followUp: Write brief notes on lipids and nucleic acids.

rubric.why: Carbohydrates are energy-providing organic compounds made mainly of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.
rubric.description: States the composition and a main function of carbohydrates.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for composition or a correct example and 1 mark for identifying their role as an energy source.

rubric.why: Proteins are made of amino acids and are important for growth and repair.
rubric.description: States the building blocks and a main function of proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for amino acids or nitrogen-containing composition and 1 mark for growth, repair or another valid protein function.

modelAnswer: Carbohydrates are organic compounds made mainly of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.
They are an important source of energy; glucose is a simple carbohydrate, while starch and glycogen are storage carbohydrates.
Proteins are organic compounds made of amino acids and contain carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen.
Proteins are needed for growth and repair and also form enzymes and some structural components of cells.

items.followUp: Define hypertension and describe one cause and one possible effect.

rubric.why: Cardiovascular disorders affect the heart and/or blood vessels.
rubric.description: Defines cardiovascular disorders.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying disorders of the heart and blood vessels.

rubric.why: A myocardial infarction occurs when blood flow and oxygen supply to part of the heart muscle are severely reduced, usually by a blocked coronary artery.
rubric.description: Explains the cause and effect of myocardial infarction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for blockage of a coronary artery and 1 mark for reduced oxygen supply causing damage or death of heart muscle.

rubric.why: Chest pain and accompanying symptoms are common signs of a heart attack.
rubric.description: Gives symptoms of myocardial infarction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for severe chest pain and 1 mark for another valid symptom, such as sweating, nausea or pain spreading to the arm.

modelAnswer: Cardiovascular disorders are diseases or abnormalities of the heart and blood vessels.
Myocardial infarction, or a heart attack, occurs when a coronary artery becomes blocked, commonly by a blood clot forming over a fatty deposit.
The blockage reduces the supply of oxygenated blood to part of the heart muscle, causing its cells to become damaged or die.
A person may experience severe chest pain, which can spread to the arm, as well as sweating or nausea.
Myocardial infarction is a medical emergency.

items.followUp: Define an organ and give one example.

rubric.why: A tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform a particular function.
rubric.description: Defines tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a group of similar cells performing a common function.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates understanding of the definition.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid tissue example.

modelAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a particular function.
Xylem is an example of a tissue.

items.followUp: Differentiate between an organ and an organ system.

rubric.why: Morphology deals with the external form and structure of organisms.
rubric.description: Defines morphology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying morphology as the study of external form or structure.

rubric.why: Anatomy deals with internal structure.
rubric.description: Defines anatomy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying anatomy as the study of internal structure.

modelAnswer: Morphology is the study of the external form and structure of an organism.
Anatomy is the study of the internal structure of an organism.
